process_area.title: Multi-Element Arrangement Identification & Performance Obligation Assessment

fields.Participants: Controller, CFO, Channel owners (VS-10/11/13/45/47/48/53/54/92/95/142/154/155/156), Tax (VS-79), External Auditor
fields.Trigger: New channel/revenue stream; quarterly close; annual policy refresh
fields.Volume: 1 enterprise revenue-stream register; ~20+ distinct revenue types across 5 entities

Automation Opportunity: - Contract/revenue-stream register auto-populated from ERP contract & channel modules; GL-revenue-account coverage exception report; change-detection alert when a channel posts a new revenue GL
Controls: - CTL-701 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Element Arrangement Identification & Performance Obligation Assessment (PA-157.1).)
- CTL-701: every revenue stream has a documented PFRS 15 decision (links VS-21 financial-controls audit); register reconciled to GL quarterly; new streams gated by W4645
Cross-references: - elevates W487 (VS-15.1); links to VS-17.1 (GL), VS-13/VS-54 (loyalty/gift card), W4643 (disclosure), W4645 (new-stream gate)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Shadow-revenue risk**: A new stream (e.g., a Pass-17 service) books revenue with no PFRS 15 decision on record → mis-recognition accumulates silently; mitigated by register-to-GL reconciliation and the W4645 pre-launch gate
- **Orphan-account risk**: GL revenue accounts with no owning stream hide errors; mitigated by account-to-stream mapping and quarterly reconcile
System Touchpoints: - ERP Revenue/Contract module (revenue-stream master, performance-obligation tags); GL account mapping (links VS-17.1); legacy W487 register (VS-15.1); channel subledgers (VS-10/13/54)
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 days/quarter register maintenance + reconcile; absorbed in Revenue Accounting

steps.activity: Revenue Accounting maintains the enterprise revenue-stream & contract-portfolio register: each stream mapped to (a) owning channel/VS, (b) entity, (c) PFRS 15 treatment summary, (d) performance obligation(s), (e) recognition trigger, (f) gross/net posture, (g) deferred vs. current, (h) disclosure category

Each channel owner confirms its streams (POS cash-and-carry, BOPIS, delivery, installation, subscription, retail media, marketplace commission, consignment sell-through, gift card, loyalty, trade-in, COD, VAS/bills-payment, construction-finance referral) are captured and unchanged/changed

Revenue Accounting reconciles the register to GL revenue accounts and to the W487 legacy scenario list; flags any stream lacking a documented PFRS 15 decision or any GL account lacking an owning stream

fields.Frequency: Per significant contract + periodic review of template contracts
fields.Trigger: New/custom contract; contract modification; bundling of separate contracts

Automation Opportunity: - Contract-clause extraction to flag combination/modification triggers; modification decision-template workflow linked to the project module
Controls: - CTL-701 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Element Arrangement Identification & Performance Obligation Assessment (PA-157.1).)
- CTL-701: contract-identification decision documented for atypical arrangements; modification classification reviewed by Controller; Legal sign-off on combined-contract conclusions
Cross-references: - links to VS-100.3 (legal/contracts), VS-11.2/VS-46.2 (project/B2B), VS-66 (design), W4577/W4553/W4265 (Pass-17 streams), W4641 (close)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-combined-contracts risk**: Treating one commercial deal as several contracts (or vice versa) mis-allocates the transaction price across obligations; mitigated by Legal+Accounting joint assessment and documented criteria

- **Modification mis-classification risk**: A change order treated as a new contract when it should be a cumulative catch-up (or the reverse) distorts period revenue; mitigated by the modification-decision template
System Touchpoints: - Contract lifecycle (VS-100.3); project/job module (VS-11.2); revenue-stream register (W4625); modification journal (VS-17.1)
Time Estimate: - ~1–3 hours per complex contract; ~5–10 days/yr aggregate for combinations/modifications

steps.activity: Revenue Accounting/Legal determine whether a contract exists under PFRS 15 (enforceable rights/obligations, commercial substance, collectibility probable) for atypical arrangements (trade-in W4577, construction-finance referral W4553, COD W4265, design-service MOUs VS-66)

Assess contract combination (multiple contracts with same customer entered near in time with single commercial objective — common in project/B2B VS-11/VS-46) and contract modification (change-scope/price — is it a separate contract or a cumulative catch-up?)
Document the identification/combination/modification conclusion and the resulting performance-obligation remeasurement; route consequential changes to W4641 close cycle and W4645 if a new pattern

fields.Frequency: Per bundle SKU/service combo + annual review
fields.Trigger: New bundle/kit launch (VS-92); installation-with-product sale (VS-12); design+build (VS-66)
fields.Volume: ~300–500 kit/bundle SKUs in catalog; every product+install sale (VS-12)

workflows.name: Performance-Obligation Identification for Bundled Product + Service Arrangements

Automation Opportunity: - Performance-obligation tagging on the kit/BOM master; auto-split of bundle revenue at POS based on obligation tags
Controls: - CTL-701 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Element Arrangement Identification & Performance Obligation Assessment (PA-157.1).)
- CTL-701: distinct-obligation assessment documented per bundle; recognition-timing criteria checklist; obligation tags reviewed at kit setup
Cross-references: - links to VS-92 (kitting), VS-12 (installation), VS-66 (design), VS-01.1 (assortment), W544 (service work order), W4634 (allocation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden-service-in-product risk**: Recognizing the entire bundle at product delivery overstates period revenue when installation is a separate obligation not yet complete; mitigated by obligation split at the SKU/work-order level

- **Over-time mis-application risk**: Applying over-time recognition to installation that does not meet the no-alternative-use/right-to-payment test → premature revenue; mitigated by the criteria checklist
System Touchpoints: - Kit/BOM module (VS-92.1); service work order (W544); POS/order-to-cash posting (VS-08/VS-16); revenue obligation tags
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 hours per new bundle/combo; ~3–5 days/yr aggregate

steps.activity: For each bundle (VS-92) and product+installation sale (VS-12), identify the distinct performance obligations: is the product distinct from the installation service? Is the design service (VS-66) distinct from materials? Apply the "distinct" criteria (capable of being used alone; identifiable in the contract)

Determine recognition timing per obligation: product = point in time (delivery/POS, control transfer); installation = point in time (completion) or over-time if it creates an asset with no alternative use + right to payment; design = over-time/point-in-time per terms
Tag the kit/BOM (VS-92.1) and the service-work-order (W544) with the performance-obligigation structure so POS/order posting routes revenue to the correct obligation and period

fields.Participants: Channel owners (VS-48/95/156/142/154/155), Legal (VS-100.3), Tax (VS-79), Controller, External Auditor
fields.Trigger: New marketplace/retail-media/VAS/COD flow; annual gross/net review

workflows.name: Principal-vs-Agent (Gross-vs-Net) Determination for Marketplace, Retail Media, VAS & COD

Automation Opportunity: - Principal-vs-agent decision template with indicator scoring; auto-routing of commission vs. gross revenue at the transaction per the decision
Controls: - CTL-701 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Element Arrangement Identification & Performance Obligation Assessment (PA-157.1).)
- CTL-701: documented indicator-based principal-vs-agent decision per flow (reviewed by External Auditor); system posting matches the conclusion; re-assessed annually
Cross-references: - links to VS-48 (retail media), VS-95 (marketplace), VS-156 (VAS agency), VS-142 (COD), VS-154 (construction finance), VS-155 (trade-in), W4643 (disclosure), W4645 (gate)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Gross-vs-net error risk**: Mis-stating a net commission flow as gross inflates reported revenue (and COGS) — a top external-audit focus (the group is privately held; no SEC disclosure regime applies); mitigated by the documented indicator analysis and annual re-assessment
- **Inconsistent-posting risk**: A gross/net conclusion not reflected in system posting → books diverge from the accounting decision; mitigated by IT config + Controller sign-off
System Touchpoints: - Marketplace/retail-media/VAS/COD subledgers; POS/ecommerce revenue posting (VS-08/VS-10); GL gross-vs-net account structure; disclosure schedule (W4643)
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 days per new flow decision; ~3–5 days annual re-assessment across all flows

steps.activity: For each flow where BuildRight sits between a third party and a customer (marketplace 3P seller VS-95, retail media VS-48, VAS/financial-agency VS-156, COD VS-142, construction-finance referral VS-154, trade-in resale VS-155), apply the principal-vs-agent indicators: control of the good/service before transfer; primary obligor; inventory risk; pricing discretion; credit risk

Conclude gross (recognize full revenue + offsetting cost) vs. net (recognize only commission/fee) and document the rationale + indicator evidence; for VAS (VS-156) confirm BuildRight is agent of the principal; for marketplace confirm BuildRight is platform operator (net on commission)
Configure the ERP/POS/ecommerce posting to gross or net per the conclusion; reflect in the disclosure schedule (W4643) and re-assess annually or on flow change

fields.Volume: ~300 VMI/consignment SKUs from 12 vendors; monthly settlements

Automation Opportunity: - Sell-through-triggered auto-posting of consignment revenue + vendor payable; exception dashboard for unmatched sell-through
Controls: - CTL-701 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Element Arrangement Identification & Performance Obligation Assessment (PA-157.1).)
- CTL-701: ownership-flag prevents premature recognition; three-way reconcile (POS × vendor settlement × consignment inventory) monthly; principal/gross posture documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-45 (consignment/VMI), W543 (sell-through trigger), VS-45.3 (settlement), VS-05 (inventory), W4647 (contract-liability reconcile)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Premature-recognition risk**: Recognizing consignment revenue at store receipt (as if purchased) overstates revenue and inventory; mitigated by the ownership-flag gate and sell-through trigger
- **Unreconciled-sell-through risk**: POS sell-through and vendor settlement mismatch → revenue or payable error; mitigated by the monthly three-way reconcile (POS × settlement × inventory)
System Touchpoints: - Consignment/VMI module (VS-45); POS sell-through trigger (W543); AP/vendor settlement (VS-45.3); consignment inventory ownership flag (VS-05)

steps.activity: Confirm revenue is NOT recognized at consignment-stock receipt (goods remain vendor-owned per VS-45.1); recognize only at customer sell-through (W543 trigger) — verify the inventory ownership flag and the sell-through feed

Compute consignment/VMI revenue at sell-through price, validate against the POS sell-through report (W543) and the vendor settlement (VS-45.3), and confirm BuildRight is principal (gross) for consignment sales to the consumer

Post revenue + AP/vendor-payable at sell-through; reconcile the consignment inventory balance (vendor-owned) against recognized revenue and the monthly vendor statement; investigate any unmatched sell-through

fields.Frequency: Per arrangement type + quarterly deposit review
fields.Trigger: Layaway/deposit transaction (VS-08/VS-11); bill-and-hold request; annual review
fields.Volume: Layaway/custom-order deposits on project & special orders (~thousands/yr); bill-and-hold rare

Automation Opportunity: - Deposit-to-deferred-revenue auto-posting; control-transfer-triggered release; contract-liability aging dashboard
Controls: - CTL-701 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Element Arrangement Identification & Performance Obligation Assessment (PA-157.1).)
- CTL-701: deposits posted to contract liability (not revenue); bill-and-hold criteria checklist; contract-liability GL reconciled to open-deposit list quarterly
Cross-references: - links to VS-08/VS-11/VS-16 (layaway/deposit/AR), W546 (project deposit), W4647 (contract-liability reconcile), W4635 (gift-card breakage — analogous deferred model)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Deposit-as-revenue risk**: Booking customer deposits as revenue at cash receipt overstates revenue and understates contract liability; mitigated by the deferred-revenue posting rule and quarterly reconcile
- **Bill-and-hold abuse risk**: Recognizing bill-and-hold revenue without meeting all criteria → premature revenue (a classic audit finding); mitigated by the mandatory criteria checklist
System Touchpoints: - Layaway/deposit module (VS-08/VS-11/VS-16); contract-liability GL (VS-17.1); project deposit W546; AR (VS-16)
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 days/quarter deposit/contract-liability reconciliation; bill-and-hold cases ad-hoc

steps.activity: Assess revenue recognition for customer deposits & layaway: deposit = contract liability (deferred) until control transfers (delivery for layaway; milestone for project deposits W546); do NOT recognize at cash receipt

For bill-and-hold (customer pays but asks BuildRight to hold inventory), apply the PFRS 15 criteria (commercial reason, segregated, ready for transfer, timing fixed) before recognizing at billing rather than delivery
Reconcile the customer-deposit/contract-liability GL balance to the open layaway/deposit/POU (point-of-use) list quarterly; release to revenue at the control-transfer trigger

fields.Participants: Loyalty (VS-13), Marketing (VS-14), Actuarial/Analytics, Controller, External Auditor
fields.Trigger: Loyalty program change (VS-13); new reward tier/partner; annual fair-value refresh
fields.Volume: 1 loyalty program; 600K members; ~ points earned on every one of 2.8M monthly POS transactions

workflows.name: Loyalty-Points, Rewards & Deferred-Revenue Performance Obligation Setup

Automation Opportunity: - Transaction-price auto-allocation to points at POS; engine-to-GL auto-reconcile with exception routing; redemption-triggered revenue release
Controls: - CTL-701 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Element Arrangement Identification & Performance Obligation Assessment (PA-157.1).)
- CTL-701: documented SSP/breakage methodology (External-Auditor reviewed); engine-to-GL monthly reconcile; estimate refreshed quarterly
Cross-references: - links to VS-13 (loyalty), W104/W17 (points liability), W4633/W4636 (SSP/breakage measurement), W4647 (reconcile), W4643 (disclosure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Actuarial-estimation risk**: The points fair value and breakage rate drive a material deferred-revenue balance and are estimation-heavy → audit scrutiny and period volatility; mitigated by documented methodology (W4636) and quarterly true-up
- **Engine-to-GL drift risk**: Loyalty-engine points liability and GL deferred revenue diverge → mis-statement; mitigated by monthly reconcile
System Touchpoints: - Loyalty engine (VS-13 W17/W104); POS earning feed (VS-08); deferred-revenue GL (VS-17.1); redemption feed
Time Estimate: - ~3–5 days/quarter points accounting + estimate refresh; monthly ~1 day reconcile

steps.activity: Confirm loyalty points are a separate performance obligation (distinct from the underlying sale); allocate a portion of the transaction price to points at each earning transaction based on standalone selling price (W4633/W4636) — defer that portion
Set the breakage/forfeiture estimate and the points fair value; recognize deferred revenue to revenue when points are redeemed (or expire/forfeit) per W4636; review the estimate each period
Reconcile the points-deferred-revenue GL to the loyalty-engine points liability (W104/W17) and the redemption feed monthly; investigate redemption-rate drift

fields.Participants: Trade/Government sales (VS-11/VS-46), Project Finance, Controller, Tax (VS-79), External Auditor
fields.Volume: ~ Project/B2B/G2G contracts (VS-11/VS-46); material project revenue (~30% trade + 10% corporate)

Automation Opportunity: - Cost-to-cost % complete auto-computation from the project module; contract asset/liability auto-derivation from billings-vs-revenue; onerous-contract trigger on margin breach
Controls: - CTL-701: documented over-time/point-in-time decision per contract; measure-of-progress reviewed by Controller; contract asset/liability reconciled monthly; onerous-contract provision assessed each period
Cross-references: - links to VS-11.2/VS-46.2 (project/government), W165/W1288 (progress billing), W918 (project margin), W4641 (close), W4643 (disclosure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Measure-of-progress error risk**: An inappropriate input/output measure mis-states period revenue (front-loading or back-loading); mitigated by documented method selection and periodic review

- **Onerous-contract miss risk**: Failing to recognize a PAS 37 onerous-contract provision on a loss project understates the liability; mitigated by the periodic onerous check tied to margin monitoring (VS-11.2 W918)
- **Billings-vs-revenue drift risk**: Billings and revenue diverge without a clean contract asset/liability split → cut-off errors; mitigated by monthly reconcile
System Touchpoints: - Project/job module (VS-11.2); progress billing (W165/W1288); contract asset/liability GL (VS-17.1); government module (VS-46)
Time Estimate: - ~3–6 days/quarter project/government revenue accounting + measure-of-progress review; per-contract ~2–4 hours

steps.activity: For project/government contracts (VS-11.2/VS-46.2), assess over-time recognition: does BuildRight create an asset with no alternative use AND an enforceable right to payment for performance to date? If both → over-time (input/output measure of progress); else point-in-time at delivery/handover

Select and document the measure of progress (cost-to-cost input method typical for project supply; output/milestone if more faithful); compute % complete, contract revenue, and the onerous-contract check (PAS 37) each period

Reconcile over-time/point-in-time revenue to billings (W165/W1288 progress billing) and the contract asset/liability (billed-but-unrecognized vs. recognized-but-unbilled); investigate cumulative catch-up at each measurement date
